hide-desktop: Changes desktop icon visibility. Linux is not supported.
lock-screen: macOS uses display sleep; immediate password protection depends on your OS settings.
break-time: Notifications require permission. Full-screen activity detection is best effort.
sleep-timer: Explicit confirmation before arming a power action. Cancel from the launcher banner.
window-on-top: Windows native window controls; some protected applications may refuse changes.
window-manager: Windows native window controls; minimum window sizes can constrain layouts.
show-desktop: Windows only. Restores the windows tracked by this session.
close-apps: Requests normal window closure after review. Applications may show their own save prompts.
focus-window: Windows dimming overlays; multi-monitor runtime acceptance is still open.
switch-resolution: Windows only. A confirmation countdown automatically requests rollback if you do not keep the mode.
eject-volumes: Windows only. Busy or protected devices can refuse an eject request.
energy-saver: Selects an available Windows power plan; available plans depend on the device.
hidden-files: Uses file-manager settings on Windows and macOS; changing macOS settings can restart Finder.
cpu-temperature: Only sensors exposed by the system are available. Many Windows devices expose none.
presentation-mode: Combines keep-awake with supported desktop controls. Notification settings remain manual OS controls.
do-not-disturb: Opens supported OS settings. You change the notification mode yourself.
airplane-mode: Opens Windows airplane-mode settings. You control the radios in Windows.
alarm: Requires notification permission and Oxbox to remain running; the app does not wake a powered-off computer.
date-countdown: Uses explicit time zones. Notifications require permission and a running app.
mute-microphone: Windows default input device; Linux requires a working pactl/PulseAudio-compatible server.
record-audio: Requires your own FFmpeg installation, a supported input device, and OS permission.
record-screen: Requires FFmpeg. Linux recording currently uses X11; macOS and Wayland recording are unavailable through this provider.
make-gif: Requires your own FFmpeg installation. Converts a selected local video segment.
convert-audio-video: Requires your own FFmpeg installation. Available codecs depend on that build.
take-photo: Requires FFmpeg, a supported camera and OS camera permission.
take-video: Requires FFmpeg and camera permission. Camera recording does not include microphone audio.
recognize-text: Windows OCR uses installed language packs. Other platforms require user-installed Tesseract and language data.
measure-color: Local-image sampling works without screen permission; screen sampling inherits capture restrictions.
currency-converter: Import dated reference rates locally, or explicitly opt into a manual ECB HTTPS refresh. Reference rates are not live trading quotes.
mouse-activity: Windows only. Starts only when you choose, moves the pointer while idle, and yields when input resumes. Stop from the app or tray.
